content_metadata.description: Video documenting an anti-nuclear protest, focusing on the dangers of nuclear power through an interview with Rick and the presentation of a letter to the Japanese Consulate.

qAndA.question: Who is the letter being addressed to?
According to Rick, where is the radioactive waste in Hanford from?

qAndA.answer: He believes that radiation is deadly no matter how much there is, stating even the smallest particle will kill eventually.
qAndA.question: What is Rick's opinion on the safety of any amount of radiation?
What visual element in the background might symbolize the lasting impacts of decisions related to nuclear power?
What does the Interviewer encourage viewers to do by showing the contact information for Eugene Peaceworks?

activities.description: Interviewer introduces the location, the people she is with, and the letter they are delivering.
Interviewer shows the letter to the camera and points out contact information for Eugene Peaceworks.
Interviewer asks Rick three questions about Fukushima, Hanford, and radiation.

characterInteraction.description: The Interviewer directs the conversation, guiding Rick to answer specific questions about nuclear power.
The Interviewer engages in a Q&A session with Rick.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene introduces the context of a protest against nuclear power, focusing on the dangers of Fukushima and Hanford through the perspective of Rick and a letter to the Japanese Consulate.

mood.description: Neutral, Curious. The scene is informative as the Interviewer explains the situation and introduces Rick. The mood is slightly curious as she prepares to ask Rick questions.

narrativeProgression.description: The Interviewer introduces the setting and the purpose of the video, mentioning the Capitol building and the protest.
She introduces Rick Gold and mentions Eugene Peaceworks and their letter to the Japanese Consulate.
The Interviewer shows the camera a letter addressed to the Japanese Consulate, explaining its purpose.
The Interviewer begins asking Rick a series of questions related to nuclear power.

scenes.thematicElements: Anti-nuclear activism, environmental concerns, government accountability, public awareness.

youtube_description:
Eugene PeaceWorks joined us at the Oregon State Capitol Yesterday
to commemorate the 4th year that Fukushima changed the world.

Our world leaders have exacerbated to situation in Fukushima by pretending "it's business as usual".

Thanks for caring Rick.
